Chapter 01 Reading 1 독감 주사, 왜 해마다 맞아야 할까?
The flu is a common illness that spreads easily during the winter.
The best way to protect yourself is to get a flu shot.
The flu shot contains a dead version of the virus.
It cannot make you sick, but it is enough for your body to practice fighting it.
When this virus enters your body, your defense system creates special protectors called antibodies.
These protectors are designed to recognize and attack the virus in the future.
It usually takes about two weeks to produce enough of them to protect your body effectively.
After this, if the real flu virus enters your body, the antibodies can destroy it quickly.
As a result, you may have only a mild illness or not feel sick at all.
However, one shot does not last long.
The number of antibodies in your body goes down over time, and the flu virus changes a little bit every year.
Therefore, you must get a new flu shot every year to stay fully protected.
Chapter 01 Reading 2 운동 두 가지, 몸에는 어떻게 다를까?
People exercise to feel healthier and stronger.
Two common ways to do this are aerobic exercise and strength training.
Aerobic exercise includes activities like running or swimming, which keep your body moving for a long time.
As you move, you breathe faster, and your lungs take in more oxygen from the air.
Your heart also beats more quickly to deliver oxygen-rich blood throughout your body.
Over time, these exercises strengthen your heart and lungs.
Try this for about an hour, six to seven days a week, to keep your body active.
Strength training, on the other hand, involves short, intense exercises like push-ups or lifting weights.
It challenges your muscles to work harder, helping them grow stronger.
Try this two or three times a week, leaving rest days in between so your muscles can recover.
Both types of exercise help your body in different ways, so keep a balanced routine to get the most benefits.
Chapter 01 Reading 3 손만 씻었는데 산모들이 살았다고?
In the 1840s, Ignaz Semmelweis, a doctor in Austria, noticed that many mothers in his hospital died from a fever after childbirth.
To find out why, he considered possible reasons.
As he observed the doctors at work, he noticed that many doctors did autopsies and then helped deliver babies without washing their hands.
He wondered if something harmful was being passed from the dead bodies to mothers.
Soon, a tragic event gave him clear evidence.
A colleague cut his finger during an autopsy and later died with the same symptoms as the mothers.
After this, he ordered doctors in his hospital to wash their hands with chlorinated lime before helping with births.
As a result, the death rate dropped sharply, from 18% to 1%.
Despite this success, other doctors refused to believe him because the idea of germs had not yet been discovered.
His advice was only recognized after his death.
Today, handwashing is known as one of the most effective ways to prevent disease.
Chapter 01 Reading 4 과자 봉지 뒷면 표, 이렇게 읽으면 된다
When you buy packaged food, you can find a Nutrition Facts label on the package.
This label provides information about the food you are eating.
At the top, it indicates the serving size, which tells you the amount for one serving.
All the numbers on the label are based on this amount.
If you eat two servings, you must double all the other numbers!
Next, the label displays calories to show how much energy the food provides.
Too many calories can cause weight gain.
Below the calories, you will find a list of nutrients like fats, protein, and vitamins.
Next to each nutrient, the Percent Daily Value (%DV) is shown to explain how much a nutrient in one serving contributes to your daily needs.
For example, if a bowl of cereal contains 30% DV of fiber, it means one serving gives about one-third of the fiber your body needs in a day.
By checking the label, you can make healthier food choices.
Chapter 02 Reading 1 색 가루를 뿌리면 모두가 똑같아진다고?
Every year in early spring, India comes alive with the festival of Holi.
Holi is known around the world as the “Festival of Colors,” which celebrates the arrival of spring and new beginnings.
For the main celebration, people gather outside and fill the streets with music and laughter.
They sing, dance, and join in the fun as they throw colorful powders into the air and splash water on friends, family, and even strangers.
But Holi is more than a fun celebration.
When everyone is covered in bright powders, differences in age, wealth, or social status seem to disappear.
This experience of looking alike creates a feeling of equality and harmony.
The act of gently putting color on someone also makes it easier to smile, talk, and have fun together.
Many people use this moment to forget old arguments.
For many, Holi is a time to share warm wishes with others and start their relationships fresh.
Chapter 02 Reading 2 에티오피아는 왜 아직 과거에 살고 있을까?
Step into Ethiopia, and you’ll feel like you are traveling back in time.
The Ethiopian calendar is about 7 or 8 years behind the rest of the world.
This is because Ethiopia follows its own ancient calendar.
While many countries count their years from the date they believe Jesus was born, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church uses a traditional method that sets this date several years later.
This difference makes the year of the Ethiopian calendar seem behind that of the international calendar.
The structure of this calendar is unique as well.
It has 12 months of exactly 30 days each.
Since this makes only 360 days, a short 13th month with 5 or 6 days is added to complete the year.
Even the start of the year is different.
Ethiopia celebrates its New Year on Meskerem 1, which falls on September 11 or 12 on the international calendar.
For Ethiopians, this unique calendar is a part of their identity and reflects traditions that have been passed down for centuries.
Chapter 02 Reading 3 슈퍼볼, 경기 말고 다들 뭘 볼까?
Every February, the United States comes alive for the Super Bowl, the championship game of American football.
It began in 1967 as a contest between two leagues, but it has grown into one of the biggest annual events in the U.S.
One reason for the Super Bowl’s huge appeal is its format.
Because there is only one game to decide the champion, the event is filled with drama and high-pressure moments.
This keeps viewers excited throughout the match.
But the game is only part of the experience.
The halftime show brings famous artists, dancers, and special effects, almost like a concert in the middle of a sports event.
The commercials are just as famous.
Each 30-second advertisement costs millions of dollars, so companies make creative advertisements that people talk about long after the game.
With so much excitement packed into one day, Super Bowl Sunday feels almost like a holiday.
Families and friends gather for parties filled with snacks, music, and games.
These parties turn the sports event into a shared celebration across the country.
Chapter 02 Reading 4 덴마크에서는 아이 이름을 마음대로 못 짓는다고?
In many countries, parents can name their children whatever they like.
But in Denmark, names must follow special guidelines set by the government.
Parents in Denmark must choose from an official list of over 18,000 approved names.
Each name is marked as male, female, or unisex, and it has to follow Danish spelling rules.
Names that are considered rude, very unusual, or likely to cause problems, like Monkey, are not allowed.
But what about parents from other cultures who want a name that reflects their family heritage?
If their preferred name is not on the list, they can apply for approval through a government agency.
Each year, over 1,100 names are reviewed this way.
While these naming laws might seem strict, they are meant to protect children from shame, confusion, or even bullying.
Beyond that, the rules reflect Denmark’s effort to preserve cultural identity.
Chapter 03 Reading 1 누구는 향긋, 누구는 비누? 고수 맛의 비밀
Do you like cilantro?
It is a popular herb used in many dishes around the world.
Some people love its fresh flavor and smell, but others really dislike it.
This is not only about personal preference.
Scientists say this difference is partly due to our genes.
Cilantro contains aldehydes, chemicals that give it a sharp, soapy scent.
Everyone carries a gene called OR6A2 that detects these chemicals.
However, some people have a variation of this gene that makes them more sensitive to aldehydes.
As a result, cilantro tastes like soap to them.
But genes explain only part of this difference.
What you eat while growing up and your culture may also affect whether you enjoy the flavor of cilantro.
So if you think cilantro tastes bad, it might be because of both your genes and experiences, not just picky eating!
Chapter 03 Reading 2 얼음인데 녹지 않는다? 드라이아이스의 두 얼굴
Dry ice may look like regular ice, but it has very different properties.
Regular ice is made of frozen water, but dry ice is the solid form of carbon dioxide.
Because of this, dry ice becomes extremely cold and can reach temperatures as low as -78.5°C.
It also doesn’t melt into a liquid.
Instead, it changes directly from a solid into a gas.
This is why it is called “dry” ice.
These special properties make dry ice useful in many situations.
It is often used to keep food and medicine fresh during shipping.
Dry ice also creates an eye-catching effect.
When the cold gas from dry ice meets moisture in the air, it forms a white fog.
This fog is often used in movies, concerts, and stage performances.
However, dry ice must be handled safely.
Touching it with bare hands can freeze the skin instantly.
Also, the gas it releases can build up in small spaces and make it hard to breathe.
For safety, it should be handled with gloves and used in open places.
Chapter 03 Reading 3 가만히 서 있는 식물, 씨앗은 어떻게 여행할까?
Plants stay in one place for their entire lives, but their seeds must travel to survive.
If all the seeds grow near the parent plant, they will compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients.
To prevent this, plants have developed various ways to spread their seeds.
Some plants rely on wind.
These seeds are light and often have soft hairs or thin wings that help them ride the wind.
For example, dandelion seeds float like tiny parachutes, while maple seeds spin through the air due to their wing-like shape.
Other seeds travel by water.
These seeds often have hard shells to protect them during long journeys.
Coconuts can cross oceans and survive until they reach a suitable place to grow.
Animals also play a key role in spreading seeds.
Burdock seeds have small hooks that attach to animal fur and later fall off in distant areas.
Apple seeds are inside the fruit, and when animals eat the fruit, the seeds pass through their bodies and are dropped in new places.
Chapter 03 Reading 4 참치는 붉고 대구는 하얀 이유는?
When you look at different kinds of fish, you may notice that their flesh comes in different colors.
Some fish have white flesh, while others are red or orange.
These differences are closely related to how the fish live and move.
Inside a fish’s muscles, there is a reddish protein called myoglobin.
Myoglobin stores and delivers oxygen to the muscles to help them produce energy.
Fish like tuna and mackerel swim constantly and travel long distances, so they need a steady supply of oxygen to their muscles.
Because of this, their muscles contain a high level of myoglobin, which makes their flesh a deep red color.
In contrast, many fish remain still for most of the day and move only when they must escape danger or catch prey.
Since their muscles demand far less oxygen, they contain only a small amount of myoglobin.
As a result, their flesh looks pale or white.
Fish such as cod and flatfish are examples of this.
Chapter 04 Reading 1 아마존 정글에서 찾은 플라스틱을 먹는 곰팡이
In 2011, a group of Yale University students joined a research trip to the Amazon rainforest.
They wanted to collect microbes living inside plants and see what special abilities they might have.
They chose the Amazon because its warm and wet climate supports many microbes that scientists have never studied before.
Back at their university lab, the students grew the microbes and tested how they acted with different materials.
During these tests, they made a surprising discovery.
One sample contained a fungus that could break down polyurethane, a very common kind of plastic.
The fungus released special chemicals that cut the plastic into smaller pieces.
Then it absorbed those pieces and used them as energy, almost like food.
This discovery is very important because polyurethane hardly breaks down and stays in landfills for a very long time.
Today, scientists are discovering more plastic-eating fungi and studying how their abilities can be used in real life.
One day, these tiny life forms may help fight plastic pollution.
Chapter 04 Reading 2 밤하늘 별은 어디로 사라졌을까?
Have you seen a faint glow spreading over buildings at night?
This glow comes from light pollution.
It happens when artificial light from streetlights, buildings, and signs shines upward and spreads through the air.
Because of this, it hides the stars and makes them difficult to see.
But this isn’t just about stargazing.
Light pollution harms animals and people, too.
Some birds that use stars for navigation can get lost.
Likewise, baby sea turtles, which follow the moonlight to the ocean after hatching, are often pulled in the wrong direction by bright city lights.
For humans, darkness is important for our bodies to rest.
Too much light at night confuses our body clocks, which can cause sleep problems and increase the risk of heart disease.
The good news is that we can reduce this problem.
We can use lights that shine downward and use timers or sensors to turn them off when not needed.
These small changes can help bring back stars and healthier nights.
Chapter 04 Reading 3 약을 싱크대에 버리면 어떤 일이 생길까?
Many people throw away unused or expired medicine in the trash or wash it down the sink.
If these strong drug chemicals leak into the soil or water, normal cleaning systems cannot remove them.
This causes serious problems.
For example, hormone medicines can damage aquatic ecosystems.
They can even turn male fish into female fish.
This change makes it difficult for fish to reproduce, and their population can decrease.
Certain drugs, such as antibiotics, can cause another problem.
When these drugs enter the environment, bacteria in water and soil are exposed to them over long periods of time.
Because the chemicals are too weak to kill the bacteria, some survive.
Over time, they develop resistance to antibiotics and become harder to kill.
These bacteria can spread through water, soil, or animals and reach people.
When they cause infections, the sickness becomes harder to treat.
To prevent these problems, we must use pharmacy return boxes or local take-back programs to dispose of medicine safely.
Chapter 04 Reading 4 바다가 오르내리는 힘으로 전기를 만든다고?
The water in the ocean rises and falls in a steady rhythm, and this movement creates tides.
These tides move huge amounts of water in and out of bays with great force.
This natural movement can be used to generate electricity.
This idea is called tidal power.
One common way to generate tidal power is to use a tidal barrage, a dam built at the entrance of a bay.
The barrage has turbines and generators, and the moving water provides the energy to turn them.
During high tide, water from the sea flows through the dam into a basin and spins the turbines.
As the turbines spin, they drive the generators to produce electricity.
After the basin fills, the gates are closed to hold the water.
When the tide goes out, the gates open again.
The stored water rushes back to the sea and turns the turbines a second time, once again powering the generators.
Because the tides repeat every day, tidal barrages can produce clean and renewable energy without burning fuel.
Chapter 05 Reading 1 선물 하나 받았을 뿐인데, 서재까지 바뀐 이유?
Have you ever bought something new and felt a strong desire to replace all the things you own to match it?
This pattern is called the Diderot Effect.
It comes from the story of Denis Diderot, an 18th-century French writer.
One day, he received a beautiful red robe as a gift.
It was so elegant that his other possessions suddenly seemed old and mismatched.
He started by replacing his chair, then his desk, and eventually his entire study.
This led him to a cycle of endless spending.
When we bring a new item into our lives, especially one of higher quality or a different style, it can create a feeling of dissatisfaction with our existing possessions.
This leads us to make unplanned purchases in an attempt to restore harmony.
The Diderot Effect shows how one purchase can quickly lead to overspending and waste.
Instead of falling into this trap, remember Diderot’s story the next time you consider a new purchase.
Chapter 05 Reading 2 가게마다 카드를 들고 다니던 시대, 한 장으로 끝낸 비결?
In the early 20th century, cash was the main way to pay for things, but carrying a lot of money was unsafe and inconvenient.
To offer a better option, many American stores began using store credit.
They gave small cards to trusted customers so they could take items home and pay later.
However, each card worked only at one store, so people who visited different shops or restaurants often needed several cards.
Over time, businesses realized there was a need for a single card that worked in many places.
A businessman named Frank McNamara saw this opportunity and started Diners Club in 1950.
The company issued a card that members could use at several New York City restaurants.
Diners Club then sent customers a single monthly bill.
The idea proved successful.
More restaurants joined, and soon hotels, shops, and airlines followed.
By the late 1950s and 1960s, banks introduced their own cards and helped create the global credit card networks used today.
Chapter 05 Reading 3 버려진 철도가 공원이 되었더니 생긴 일은?
The Meatpacking District in New York City was once a busy center for meat-processing factories and warehouses.
By the 1980s, many of those businesses had closed, and the area was left with many empty buildings.
In the early 2000s, the city began searching for ways to improve the neighborhood.
One major idea was to reuse an old elevated freight railway that had once carried goods to the factories.
Instead of removing it, they turned it into a public park called the High Line.
The park quickly became popular with locals and tourists.
As more people visited, trendy shops and restaurants moved in, and new luxury apartments were built.
Property values rose, and the area became more popular and more expensive.
However, higher rents made it harder for some longtime residents and small businesses to stay.
This kind of change, where investment improves a neighborhood but also pushes out existing communities, is called gentrification.
It shows why city growth can be both exciting and unfair at the same time.
Chapter 05 Reading 4 사지 않고 빌려 쓰는 시대, 구독 경제의 두 얼굴?
People once bought products mainly to own them.
But as digital technology has spread, consumers have begun to value convenience and variety more than ownership.
This change has led to the subscription economy, where people pay a small monthly fee to use products or services for a certain time.
These include music and movie streaming services and even furniture.
Subscriptions attract consumers by offering quick access to a wide range of options through one monthly payment.
This convenient access also allows consumers to explore new services and switch between them without worrying about owning or maintaining anything.
However, there are drawbacks, too.
If you subscribe to many services, the total monthly cost can become very high.
Also, you never truly own the items or content.
Once you stop paying the fee, your access ends right away.
Today, the subscription economy is a major part of modern life.
It offers convenience and choice, but it also requires consumers to make thoughtful decisions about what they pay for.
Chapter 06 Reading 1 조용한 속삭임이 몸에 일으키는 변화는?
Do you enjoy quiet whispers or tapping sounds?
If so, you might enjoy ASMR.
ASMR is a pleasant tingling feeling triggered by certain sounds.
Common ASMR triggers include whispering, tapping, crinkling materials, and brushing sounds.
Many people watch ASMR videos to relax, reduce stress, or fall asleep more easily.
But can ASMR actually affect the body and brain?
To find out, scientists experimented with 38 young adults.
They showed the participants ASMR videos and measured their heart rate, mood, and brain activity before and after watching.
The results were interesting.
Almost 40% of the participants said they experienced a tingling feeling during the videos.
These people showed lower levels of sadness afterward.
Most participants’ heart rates also slowed down, which means their bodies became calmer.
Brain scans revealed that they had increased focus and attention after watching.
So, ASMR may not just be something fun to watch online.
Because sometimes, a few simple sounds are all you need to feel better.
Chapter 06 Reading 2 왜 우리는 보고 싶은 것만 볼까?
Even today, some people still believe the Earth is flat.
When shown scientific explanations, they ignore the evidence and pay attention only to information that supports their belief.
This way of thinking is called confirmation bias.
Our brain prefers familiar ideas and often refuses to change our beliefs because it requires mental effort.
When information supports what we already believe, we accept it quickly, overlook errors, and remember it well.
But when information goes against our beliefs, we feel uncomfortable, look for faults, and forget it.
This tendency can lead to confirmation bias.
Confirmation bias becomes stronger online.
Algorithms recommend content based on what we already like, so we often see only one side of an issue.
This limits our understanding and increases divisions between groups.
To overcome this bias, the first step is to notice it.
Then we can question our views and consider other opinions and facts with an open mind.
This will help us think clearly and build a more balanced understanding of the world.
Chapter 06 Reading 3 메기를 넣었더니 정어리가 살아 도착한 이유는?
Long ago in Norway, fishermen faced a problem when transporting live sardines to the market.
The problem was that the sardines stayed still in the tank and soon became weak and exhausted.
The fish often died on the way.
One clever fisherman tried something new.
He placed a few catfish into the tank.
The catfish chased the sardines, forcing them to swim constantly, so they arrived at the market alive and healthy.
This strategy is known as the Catfish Effect.
Today, the term is used to describe how a little pressure or competition can keep people motivated.
In business, it shows that competition can keep people engaged and improve their performance.
Likewise, a smart classmate can push other students to study harder.
Without such pressure, people may become too relaxed and lose their drive.
The Catfish Effect, however, works best in moderation.
Too much pressure can cause stress and worsen performance, but the right amount of challenge can help us grow.
Chapter 06 Reading 4 ‘내가 틀렸나?’ 스스로를 의심하게 만드는 말의 정체는?
In a 1938 play called Gas Light, a husband secretly dims the gas lamps in the house.
When his wife notices the lights getting darker, he tells her that nothing has changed.
He repeats this again and again, so she begins to question her own senses and eventually believes that she is going crazy.
This strange story later gave rise to the word “gaslighting.”
The word refers to a harmful behavior that makes someone doubt their own thoughts and feelings.
A gaslighter may lie, deny the truth, or change a story to confuse another person and gain control.
As a result, the victim may lose confidence and start thinking, “Maybe I’m wrong,” even when they are right.
Gaslighting often happens between people who are close, like friends or family, because trust makes it easier to believe the gaslighter.
If you feel this is happening to you, trust your feelings.
Write down your thoughts and talk to a professional counselor.
Chapter 07 Reading 1 우주에서 본 지구가 우주비행사의 마음을 바꾼 이유
The U.S. and Russia have long been intense competitors in space exploration.
However, astronauts who have made the journey say that rivalry no longer matters.
When astronauts look down at Earth from space, they do not see borders or countries.
Instead, they see a tiny, beautiful blue ball like a “marble” floating in space.
This view changes their hearts deeply.
Before leaving Earth, astronauts may focus mainly on their own countries.
After viewing the planet from space, however, many come to understand that all humans share one home.
This experience often creates a strong sense of connection to all living things and helps them realize that Earth must be protected.
As a result, concern for protecting the environment and promoting world peace often grows.
Some astronauts share their changed view by writing books about their experience, and even start charities to help others.
This change in their thinking is called the Overview Effect.
It reminds us that we all live on the same small planet and encourages us to care for one another.
Chapter 07 Reading 2 우리가 보는 별빛은 이미 과거의 빛이다?
When we look at the night sky, it may seem like we are seeing the stars as they are right now.
However, we are actually seeing their past.
Light travels at about 300,000 kilometers per second, but space is so vast that even that speed isn’t enough for light to reach us instantly.
This means the starlight we observe tonight began its journey in the past.
Most stars are incredibly far away from Earth, so this delay is not just a few seconds or minutes, but often dozens or even hundreds of years.
Astronomers explain this large time delay using a unit called the light-year.
A light-year is the distance that light travels in one year.
For example, if a star is 100 light-years away, the light we see today left the star 100 years ago.
So every time we look up, we are seeing a piece of history shining in the dark sky.
Chapter 07 Reading 3 얇은 대기의 화성에서 헬리콥터가 날았다고?
Mars has a very thin atmosphere.
It is about one percent as thick as Earth’s atmosphere.
Because of this, scientists once believed that powered flight on Mars was almost impossible.
In 2021, NASA tested this belief by sending a small helicopter called Ingenuity to Mars.
The helicopter traveled to Mars on a rover and was later placed on the planet’s surface.
To fly on Mars, Ingenuity was designed to be light and powered by strong batteries.
Also, its blades were able to spin much faster than helicopters on Earth.
During its first test flight, Ingenuity lifted off using its own power.
It stayed steady in the air and then landed safely.
The flight lasted only a few seconds, but it showed that powered flight on another planet was possible.
After this success, Ingenuity completed many more flights.
These flights lasted longer and helped scientists explore Mars from the air.
Chapter 07 Reading 4 우주비행사는 어떻게 우주로 갈 준비를 할까?
At NASA’s Johnson Space Center, astronauts receive special training before traveling to space.
They begin with about two years of basic training.
During this time, they learn how the International Space Station (ISS) works and how to use and repair spacecraft equipment.
After this basic training, astronauts prepare for their specific missions.
Using full-size models of spacecraft and the space station, they practice moving, communicating, and solving problems as they would in space.
To prepare for spacewalks, they practice underwater in a huge swimming pool.
This helps them experience what it feels like to work in microgravity.
Astronauts also fly in T-38 training jets.
These fast jets help them practice making quick decisions and staying calm under pressure.
The experience prepares them for unexpected situations during space missions.
Even after all this, their training is not over.
Astronauts continue practicing for years and repeat their mission tasks many times until they are ready to fly into space.
Chapter 08 Reading 1 카드를 대기만 하면 결제가 되는 이유
Have you ever paid for a bus by tapping your card or phone?
This simple action is made possible by a wireless technology called NFC, or Near Field Communications.
NFC allows two nearby devices to share information with each other.
A card reader creates a short-range magnetic field.
When a card comes close to the reader, this field creates a small amount of electricity.
This energy activates a tiny chip inside the card, which sends your information back to the reader.
The reader then records the information and completes the payment instantly.
NFC works only at a short distance.
This is because its weak magnetic field only reaches a few centimeters.
This keeps your data safe by making it almost impossible for someone to steal it.
Today, NFC is used in many areas of daily life, such as digital wallets and smart keys.
Thanks to this technology, our daily lives have become much more convenient.
Chapter 08 Reading 2 운전대에서 손을 뗀 자동차는 어떻게 길을 찾을까?
No hands on the wheel, no feet on the pedals, just a smooth ride to school or work.
This is the idea behind self-driving cars.
They work through three main steps: sensing, thinking, and acting.
Self-driving cars rely on a variety of sensors to understand their surroundings.
Cameras read road signs, detect lanes, and recognize traffic lights.
LiDAR, a laser-based system, creates a detailed 3D map of the surroundings, while radar uses radio waves to detect objects and measure their distance and speed.
Along with its sensors, GPS helps the vehicle locate itself.
Together, these signals give the car a detailed picture of the road.
Once this data is collected, powerful computers and AI analyze it.
The system identifies objects, predicts what might happen, and responds by steering, accelerating, or braking to follow traffic rules and keep passengers safe.
Self-driving technology is advancing quickly with improvements in AI.
As the systems become better and more reliable, self-driving cars are more likely to become a part of everyday life.
Chapter 08 Reading 3 유명인이 하지도 않은 말을 하는 영상의 정체
Have you ever seen a video where a famous person said something they never actually said?
This might be a “deepfake.”
Deepfakes are realistic but fake media created with a powerful AI technique called deep learning.
Deep learning allows computers to analyze large amounts of photos, videos, and audio recordings to find patterns in faces, voices, and movements.
Using these learned patterns, the computer teaches itself to recreate a person’s image and voice in a very realistic way.
As a result, it can swap faces and alter voices in a video.
The technology has various potential applications.
For example, deepfakes can bring historical figures back to life or create complex special effects in movies.
However, not all uses of this technology are positive.
It is often used to spread false information, known as fake news, or to bully people online.
While deepfakes offer exciting new possibilities, their risks cannot be ignored.
The future of this technology depends on how responsibly we use it.
Chapter 08 Reading 4 땅속이 아닌 실험실에서 다이아몬드를 만든다고?
For a long time, diamonds could only be found deep underground.
Today, however, they can also be made in laboratories.
These are called lab-grown diamonds.
Natural diamonds form from carbon atoms deep inside the Earth.
Over millions of years, heat and pressure bond the atoms into hard crystals.
When magma rises from deep underground as a result of volcanic activity, it carries diamonds upward toward Earth’s surface.
Lab-grown diamonds copy this process.
Scientists place a tiny diamond seed in a machine that creates similar conditions.
Inside the machine, heated carbon-rich gases release carbon atoms.
These atoms settle onto the seed and build the diamond crystal layer by layer.
In the end, a real diamond is formed.
Many people choose lab-grown diamonds for several reasons.
Not only are they usually less expensive, but they also cause less damage to the environment.
They also help companies avoid moral problems related to diamond mining.
This has led to their growing popularity.
Chapter 09 Reading 1 넥타이 색과 브로치, 지도자의 옷이 하는 말은?
For many leaders, fashion is more than decoration, as it sends quiet but powerful messages to the public.
In the United States, presidents carefully choose tie colors for speeches or debates.
Red is the color of the Republican Party.
A red tie suggests confidence and strength.
Democrats often wear a blue tie, which shows calmness and trust.
Sometimes, a leader wears a purple tie to show unity between political parties.
In Britain, Queen Elizabeth II was famous for her “brooch diplomacy.”
She selected jewelry that had special meaning.
For example, when meeting Canadian leaders, she wore a maple leaf brooch.
The maple leaf is the symbol of Canada.
With this one piece of jewelry, she quietly expressed friendship and respect.
Though simple, fashion choices like these help people understand what leaders want to say and how they want to be seen.
Chapter 09 Reading 2 외교관이 체포되지 않는 이유는?
A diplomat is an official who works in a foreign country to represent their own government.
Their job is to maintain peace and build good relationships between countries through communication.
In the past, this job was dangerous.
If a diplomat delivered bad news or messages that angered the host government, they could be punished directly.
Some were accused of spying or even arrested on false charges.
These actions made it hard for countries to talk or trust one another.
To prevent this, countries created a special legal protection called diplomatic immunity.
Under this protection, diplomats are not subject to the laws of the host country.
Local police cannot arrest or jail them, even if they are suspected of breaking a law.
Because of diplomatic immunity, diplomats can avoid unjust treatment or political pressure.
They are able to speak honestly, deliver difficult messages without fear, and communicate openly, which is essential for global peace.
Chapter 09 Reading 3 버스 자리를 양보하지 않은 로자 파크스, 무슨 일이?
Sometimes, laws are unfair.
When this happens, people can use civil disobedience to make a change.
Civil disobedience is the act of peacefully breaking an unfair law to show it’s wrong.
Its purpose is to help others recognize the problem and call for change.
A famous example happened in the United States in 1955.
At that time, many laws treated Black people unfairly.
On buses, the law required Black passengers to give up their seats to white passengers.
One day in Montgomery, Alabama, a woman named Rosa Parks calmly refused to give up her seat.
Knowing the rule was unfair, she stayed seated and was arrested.
Her action became a powerful act of civil disobedience.
Rosa’s courage made many people realize how wrong the bus rules were.
Thousands of Black residents then joined the Montgomery Bus Boycott and refused to ride the buses.
After more than a year of protest, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled the bus laws illegal.
This proved that peaceful civil disobedience can change unfair laws.
Chapter 09 Reading 4 권력을 셋으로 나누는 이유는?
In a democracy, power must be shared so that no one has too much control.
This idea is called the separation of powers.
Under this system, the government is divided into three branches.
The legislative branch makes the laws.
Elected representatives propose new laws, discuss whether they are necessary and fair, and vote to decide if they should become law.
The executive branch carries out the laws.
A president or prime minister leads this branch and makes sure the laws are obeyed.
The judicial branch interprets the laws.
Judges and courts decide what the laws mean and whether people or the government have broken them.
Each branch has its own powers, but they can also check one another.
For example, the executive branch can reject a law passed by the legislative branch.
The legislative branch can review and limit how the executive branch uses its power.
The judicial branch can cancel any law that goes against the Constitution.
With this system, these branches keep power balanced and make democracy fair for everyone.
Chapter 10 Reading 1 모나리자를 유명하게 만든 도둑
Today, the Mona Lisa is one of the most famous paintings in the world.
But more than a century ago, few people had even noticed it in the Louvre Museum until one daring theft changed everything.
One morning, a man named Vincenzo Peruggia, who had once worked at the Louvre, walked into the museum wearing a worker’s uniform.
He quietly removed the painting from the wall, hid it under his coat, and walked out of the museum.
It wasn’t until the next day that anyone noticed it was gone.
The story made headlines across the world.
Shocked visitors crowded into the Louvre, staring at the empty space where it had once hung.
For more than two years, the Mona Lisa remained missing.
Then, in 1913, Peruggia tried to sell it to an art dealer in Florence, Italy.
The dealer informed the police, and the painting was finally returned.
Since then, even bigger crowds have come to see it.
Ironically, the theft turned a little-known painting into a world-famous masterpiece.
Chapter 10 Reading 2 한 시간도 안 걸린 전쟁이 있다고?
Can a war last less than an hour?
Yes!
It really happened in 1896.
The war was between Britain and Zanzibar, a small island off the east coast of Africa.
At that time, Zanzibar was under British control.
When the pro-British Sultan of Zanzibar died on August 25, his cousin Khalid took power without British approval.
Britain wanted a new Sultan who would support their control, so they ordered Khalid to step down by 9:00 a.m. on August 27.
But Khalid refused and prepared to defend the palace with about 3,000 men and cannons.
In response, the British positioned five warships in the harbor.
When the deadline passed, the ships opened fire.
In just 38 minutes, the palace was destroyed, and Khalid’s flag came down.
Khalid escaped to the German embassy, and the British quickly installed their chosen leader as the new Sultan.
This brief battle became the shortest war in history and an example of how easily a powerful country could control a smaller one in the past.
Chapter 10 Reading 3 무고한 사람들을 마녀로 몰았던 마녀사냥
From the 1400s to the 1700s, when war, hunger, and illness were common in Europe, many people believed these troubles were caused by evil magic.
These fears led to what we now call “witch hunts.”
During this time, some people were labeled as witches and blamed for bad events.
They were often poor or elderly women, or people who lived alone.
Even those who were simply different from others became targets.
To calm public fear, local leaders and churches held witch trials to punish those accused of using magic.
However, these trials were unfair.
Many people were forced to confess through threats or torture.
For nearly 300 years, thousands of innocent people lost their lives.
Although witch hunts ended long ago, the term is still used today.
It describes situations in which people are unfairly blamed because of false beliefs.
This reminds us to search for the truth before judging others and to treat everyone fairly.
Chapter 10 Reading 4 실크로드는 왜 ‘길’ 하나가 아니었을까?
More than 2,000 years ago, Chinese rulers looked beyond their borders to find new allies and trade.
Envoys traveled through Central Asia and reported on distant lands.
Merchants later followed these routes, which developed into a large trade network known as the Silk Road.
The Silk Road was not a single road.
It was a group of land and sea routes that connected China with Central Asia, India, the Middle East, and Europe.
The name “Silk Road” comes from silk, a major export from China.
China traded silk, tea, and porcelain, while the West traded glass and precious metals.
Along with goods, ideas traveled as well.
Buddhism spread from India into Central Asia, and Chinese inventions such as paper moved westward.
Through trade, people shared languages, foods, and customs.
After the 15th century, wars and new sea routes reduced the Silk Road’s importance.
However, its influence lasted for centuries, and it became an early example of global trade.
